49.14.s.en: 4. The humbled one raised to be a queen:

49.14.0.en: 22 Thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I will lift up mine hand to the Gentiles, and set up my standard to the people: and they shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. 23 And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.

49.14.1.en: If Zion lived as a humbled captive nation in a foreign land, she now returns to her homeland as a queen, whom all long to lift up on their shoulders, and to whom kings submit and before whom they bow down, licking the dust of her feet.

49.14.2.en: This is God's work in the life of the soul that sin had previously humbled: the Lord raises her up as a queen, seated at the right hand of the King, and all long to serve her.

49.14.3.en: “Thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I will lift up mine hand to the Gentiles, and set up my standard to the people” [22]. What is the lifting up of the hand but the coming of the Lord Christ into the world to stretch out His hands on the Cross and so gather the Gentiles to Himself, as He said: “And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me” (Jn 12:32)? And the standard that He sets up is “his banner over me was love” (Song 2:4), that is, the proclamation of redemption on the Cross.

49.14.4.en: By this work of salvation the Church of Christ is glorified, when it is said to her: “They shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me” [22-23].

49.14.5.en: This has been fulfilled, for kings and queens have become believers working in the Church of the Lord, such as Constantine the Great and Helena, serving the Church as a spiritual queen above all.

49.15.s.en: 5. God the Redeemer of His Church:

49.15.0.en: 24 Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? 25 But thus saith the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children. 26 And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.

49.15.1.en: These promises seemed like a fantasy to Isaiah's contemporaries, and later also to the captives; therefore God affirmed that it is He Himself who accomplishes this salvation, being the only One able to crush the mighty devil and to draw out from him those whom he had previously taken captive.

49.15.2.en: “Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? But thus saith the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children. And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob” [24-26].

49.15.3.en: So it is fitting for us to trust in God our Savior and not to be troubled before the cruelty and violence of the devil, for the Savior is able to free us from his captivity however fierce and mighty the enemy may be. He brings us back to His Church and contends with those who contend with us, that is, He leads the battle Himself; so the enemy eats his own flesh and drinks and becomes drunk as with his own blood, that is, his work returns upon his own head and he tastes the bitterness of his own violence until he loses consciousness like one who is drunk.

50.0.0.en: 1 Thus saith the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away. 2 Wherefore, when I came, was there no man? when I called, was there none to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver? behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst. 3 I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering.

50.0.1.en: When a Jew divorced his wife, even without an acceptable reason, he gave her a bill of divorcement and drove her out of his house; he could also sell her as a maidservant to his creditors (Deut 24:1-3), and he was permitted to sell his children to his creditors. But God did not do so to them. He asks the Jewish nation, which denied Him and refused to believe in Him, for its bill of divorcement, affirming to her that He did not wish to divorce her or to drive her out; rather, she divorced herself and drove herself out of the house of God, her Bridegroom, through her adultery and her abominations, and so broke the holy marriage.

50.0.2.en: “Thus saith the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away” [1].

50.0.3.en: “He came unto his own, and his own received him not” (Jn 1:11). Therefore, in a fatherly reproach, He asks those who refuse faith to show a bill of divorcement or the name of the creditor to whom He delivered His children; as if He were saying to them: I do not wish to divorce your mother, nor to sell you to anyone. She chose the devil, my enemy, as a bridegroom for herself, and you sold yourselves for the pleasures and lusts of sin, just as the Lord Christ said to His opponents: “Ye are of your father the devil” (Jn 8:44).

50.0.4.en: Abba Abraham says in Cassian's Conferences: [The very pleasures in which we delight (in sin) become a punishment for us, and the delights and enjoyments turn into something like torments for the one who pursues them.]

50.0.5.en: Origen sees that the Jewish synagogue committed adultery against the Bridegroom and killed Him (Jn 19:6, 15; Lk 23:18): [She (as a bride) rose up against her husband more than he rose up against her, he who drove her out and cast her away, rebuking her for her departure from him.]

50.1.0.en: If He drove her out, it was only because she left Him and drove herself out, so He gave her the desire of her wicked heart. The Lord Christ came as to His own house and found no one, for she had left it, taking the children with her [2]. He called her, that perhaps she might be softened toward her husband and return to Him, but she did not answer [2]; she did not welcome Him nor respond to His call, but deprived Him of all His rights as husband and father.

50.1.1.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [He speaks these things to show that we are the ones who began the desertion, and that this causes our destruction. God does not wish to leave us or to punish us; even when He punishes, He does so unwillingly, for He says: “I have no pleasure in the death of the sinner, as that he should turn and live” [(Ezek 18:32) Septuagint]. Jesus weeps over the destruction of Jerusalem as we do over our friends.]

50.1.2.en: God does not want our destruction, but seeks that we be always fervent in spirit, like a bride rejoicing in her bridegroom, and not like a rebellious wife who leaves her house. As St. John Chrysostom says: [He goes deeper, giving an example that penetrates the deepest matters, saying: “As the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee” (Isa 62:5). For love is at its height at the beginning (between the bride and bridegroom). He used this manner of speaking not to attribute anything human to Himself, but that we might sense the intensity of the burning of His true love...]

50.1.3.en: For her part, she left Him and refused to live in the joy of the everlasting heavenly wedding; but for His part, He works on their behalf as a Savior who redeems them with His life, mighty and not unable to act for their sake, for He says: “Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver? behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst. I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering” [2-3].

50.1.4.en: The Lord Himself came as to His own house to save, after He had called her through the Law and the Prophets; He came to save, and yet in mockery His maidservant nation and His own said: “He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him” (Mt 27:42).

50.1.5.en: Thus His maidservant nation mocked Him, though it was He who made for her a way through the Red Sea and the river Jordan; and at His crucifixion nature was stirred, so the sun was darkened and the moon was eclipsed, and darkness came upon the face of the earth.

50.2.0.en: 4 The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned. 5 The Lord GOD hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back. 6 I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting. 7 For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed. 8 He is near that justifieth me; who will contend with me? let us stand together: who is mine adversary? let him come near to me. 9 Behold, the Lord GOD will help me; who is he that shall condemn me? lo, they all shall wax old as a garment; the moth shall eat them up.

50.2.1.en: Some scholars and Fathers see that the speaker here is the prophet Isaiah, who declared that God gave him the tongue of the learned so that he might comfort weary souls with the living word of the Lord; this word has no fixed time but works in him every morning, giving him a spiritual ear able to listen to the divine voice [4].

50.2.2.en: * “He wakeneth (adds to) mine ear to hear” [4].

50.2.3.en: It means the addition (of the ear) which is from the Spirit... For after the Spirit gave him the heart of the prophets, he no longer had a human heart but became one with a spiritual heart, as the Apostle said: “We have the mind of Christ” (1 Cor 2:16). It is as though he says: I have received the blessing of the Spirit and have learned the things which a man cannot utter, which none of us, nor of the prophets, could comprehend by his own mind.

50.2.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * The prophet heard more than many (prophets), and so the faithful also hear more than the catechumens. Here the catechumens, too, must realize that they are not learning these things from men but are taught of God (Isa 54:13).

50.2.5.en: St. John Chrysostom If the prophet speaks of himself as having enjoyed an additional spiritual ear, perhaps this means more than many prophets enjoyed, for the prophet also speaks of himself as a type of the Lord Christ, just as David the prophet earlier spoke of himself as a type of the Messiah.

50.2.6.en: Although the Lord Christ came as a Teacher of mankind, He came as unique in this in respect of the following:

50.3.0.en: a. Being the Word of God, the Giver of wisdom, knowledge and understanding, He took on our humanity and became the Son of Man who submits and obeys. He is the Hebrew servant who of his own will came forward to his master at the Jubilee to have his ear pierced, out of His zeal for His Father's house (Ezek 21:6). Therefore He says: “The Lord GOD hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back” [5]. He offered Himself willingly not only to have His ears pierced but to lay down His life, and so He was obedient unto death, even the death of the Cross.

50.3.1.en: In His obedience that gives of itself and is full of love, He offered not only His ears to be pierced, but also His back to be beaten, His cheeks to those who plucked out the hair, and His face to shame and spitting... He offered all His life, bearing sufferings, that we the disobedient might be counted obedient in Him, and that we who suffer might find rest in Him.

50.3.2.en: * Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ is an example for us of how to suffer... By His own will He allowed them to lead Him to death, and so we see in Him the image of all goodness and immortality. In this He is an example for us; if we follow Him we shall be able to tread upon serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy.

50.4.0.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * You may say: The enemy is terrifying and dangerous and cannot be endured. Look at him again and compare him with another picture, and you will learn to despise him. For the accusations, the insults, the rebukes and the reproaches that the enemies pour out together with their plots are like a worn-out garment and wool eaten by the moth [9]... Therefore let nothing of what happens weary you; cease seeking the help of this man or that, and running after shadows, but call with persistence on Jesus whom you serve, for when He bows His head, in a moment of time all evils come to an end.

50.4.1.en: St. John Chrysostom * He chose to bear all these things only to comfort those who suffer.

50.4.2.en: St. Augustine In a clear and explicit prophecy, the prophet Isaiah spoke of the events of the Cross, saying in the words of the Savior: “I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting” [6].

50.4.3.en: * You have shown me the economy of Your compassion.

50.4.4.en: You bore the injustice of the wicked; You gave Your back to the scourges, and Your cheeks You left to the slaps. For my sake, O my Lord, You did not turn Your face from the shame of spitting.

50.4.5.en: You came to the slaughter like a lamb, even to the Cross...

50.4.6.en: The Gregorian Liturgy * That fool, how did he dare to spit in His face?!

50.4.7.en: How did you dare, O tongue, to pour out spittle...?!

50.4.8.en: How did you bear, O earth, the mockery of the Son...?!

50.4.9.en: A fearful sight, full of astonishment, that a man should see wax standing up and spitting in the face of the flame...

50.4.10.en: And this also happened for the sake of Adam, because he deserved to be spat upon, for he had fallen! And in place of the servant the Master stood up to receive all this!

50.4.11.en: He offered His face to receive the spitting, because He promised in Isaiah that He would not turn away His face from bearing the shame of spitting...!

50.4.12.en: Mar Jacob of Sarug The Lord Christ gave Himself up to sufferings to the very depths, bearing all shame and disgrace in order to complete the way of obedience for us and in our name, declaring the inability of pain and disgrace to crush the faithful, and affirming that the way of the Cross is royal and leads us into His righteousness, for He says: “I know that I shall not be ashamed. He is near that justifieth me” [7-8]. The Apostle Paul says: “The redemption that is in Christ Jesus: whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness” (Rom 3:25).

50.4.13.en: * But what does he mean by saying “to declare his righteousness”...? Not only in that He is righteous, but that He makes those who are full of the foul sores of sin righteous...

50.4.14.en: Therefore doubt not... Do not reject the righteousness of God, which is not by the works (of the Law) but by (living) faith, and is easy and open to all.

50.5.0.en: 10 Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God. 11 Behold, all ye that kindle a fire, that compass yourselves about with sparks: walk in the light of your fire, and in the sparks that ye have kindled. This shall ye have of mine hand; ye shall lie down in sorrow.

50.5.1.en: The Lord obeyed in order to call us to obedience, and so He became an example for us, and also a help in whom we hide so that we may walk the way of obedience... for He says: “Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God” [10].

50.5.2.en: It is as though whoever wishes to enjoy the light of obedience and to hearken to the voice of the Lord and His Christ should trust in Him to rescue him from the darkness of disobedience.

50.6.0.en: He likens the disobedient to those who kindle a fire of their own making [11] in order to offer to the Lord strange incense, not the incense of obedience mingled with love, but the incense of selfishness and reliance on the self... Therefore it is fitting for us not to kindle the fire of our own righteousness and human wisdom, but to receive the fire of the Holy Spirit of God, the Giver of righteousness and of obedience to the commandment.

50.6.1.en: * Let us not walk in the light of our fire [11] and the flame that we ourselves have kindled, for I know a purifying fire which Christ sent on the earth (Lk 12:49), and He Himself in a symbolic way appeared as a fire that scatters what is material in evil habits. This fire He wishes to kindle quickly, for He longs to hasten us to the doing of good.
